requirements.title: Slash editing ends data transfer for the current record
requirements.definition: A slash edit descriptor indicates the end of data transfer to or from the current record.

pending.slash-ends-current-output-record: WRITE(rec,'("A"/"B")') to character(len=1) rec(2); expect rec(1)='A' and rec(2)='B'.
pending.slash-ends-current-input-record: READ(['1','2'],'(I1/I1)') into two integers from an internal file array; expect first=1 and second=2.

requirements.title: Slash positioning for sequential or stream access skips or creates records
requirements.definition: For sequential or stream files, slash skips the rest of the current input record and positions at the next record; on output it creates a new empty following record and positions at its beginning.

pending.sequential-stream-input-skip: Source-control only: exact external sequential/stream file positioning requires file fixtures, not internal WRITE.
pending.sequential-stream-output-new-record-unas: Unassertable in this packet because it requires a connected sequential or stream file; do not infer extra positioning for unlimited-item reversion from this slash rule.

requirements.title: Slash positioning for direct access advances to the next existing record
requirements.definition: For direct access, slash increases the record number by one and positions at the beginning of that record if it exists, making it current.

S13.8.2-004 control edit descriptor fixture boundaries: Only the listed executable facets are represented. Every character-output case pre-fills the internal file variable or array with '#', asserts LEN where a character scalar is observed, and compares the whole field or assembled record with an equal-length literal so blank padding cannot hide a short oracle. The fixtures do not assert processor-defined sign or leading-zero modes, nondefault-character skipped positions, external sequential/stream/direct file positioning, diagnostics, or G0 processor-selected parameters. Mutation plans are generated with each parent source: wrong oracle, changed input value, control-descriptor removal where portable, and descriptor substitutions for T3/T4, TL2/TR2, SP/SS, DC/DP, and BN/BZ.
